title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Digit 5 Humanoid

### The Breakthrough
Agility Robotics launched Digit 5, a humanoid that merges Cassie’s legged base with an upright torso and dual arms, allowing it to lift 23 kg bins, navigate narrow aisles, and operate for 90 minutes after a 9‑minute rapid charge; the company targets mass production of up to 10 000 units per year.

### The Caveats
The announcement offers no quantitative performance data, durability results, or comparisons to existing automation, so the claim of a first practical, scalable warehouse humanoid remains unsubstantiated.

## 3D Scene Graph Mobile Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
By coupling the FOUND‑IT foundation‑model pipeline with a mobile arm, the system builds real‑time monocular 3D scene graphs that detect object changes, merge multi‑session maps, plan navigation, and execute object‑level grasps without calibrated cameras, demonstrated on a real robot for scene‑rearrangement tasks.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no comparison against existing mapping or SLAM baselines, leaving the source of reported advantages unclear.

## Blind Proprioceptive Assembly

### The Breakthrough
A proprioceptive policy that consumes only joint positions, velocities, and recent actions, trained in a procedurally generated MuJoCo simulator, achieves zero‑shot sim‑to‑real peg‑in‑hole insertion with 73 % success and outperforms visual baselines in shape generalization.

### The Caveats
Real‑world evaluation is limited to peg‑in‑hole insertion; gear meshing and nut threading remain unverified on hardware.

## TransNav Quadrotor Navigation

### The Breakthrough
TransNav uses a patch‑based point‑cloud encoder and transformer to produce a compact environment representation, outputting a finite‑horizon action plan for quadrotor obstacle avoidance; it learns without expert demonstrations and shows strong performance in both simulated and real cluttered static and dynamic scenes.

### The Caveats
The paper offers no quantitative comparison to existing navigation baselines, so its true performance advantage is uncertain.

## MOSS Amphibious Robot

### The Breakthrough
MOSS employs origami wheels that morph in 1.95 ± 0.11 s, switching between contracted and expanded shapes to cut cost of transport by up to 29 % on mud, sand, and water while remaining efficient on firm ground, demonstrated across soil‑mud‑water transitions in outdoor trials.

### The Caveats
No baseline comparison to existing robots or wheel designs is provided, leaving the claimed efficiency gains unsubstantiated.

## HUMXN Home Service Data Pipeline

### The Breakthrough
HUMXN offers free plumbing, HVAC, electrical, air‑duct and carpet‑cleaning services in three cities while equipping technicians with wearable cameras and motion sensors to capture multimodal video and motion data, creating a scalable high‑fidelity dataset for training embodied‑AI robots on real‑world skilled tasks.

### The Caveats
The announcement provides no validation that the gathered sensor data will effectively train robots, offering neither dataset quality assessment nor hardware trials.

## Foxglove SDK

### The Breakthrough
The Foxglove SDK delivers a Rust‑native core with Python and C++ bindings, supporting high‑performance multimodal data logging, MCAP file handling, and live WebSocket streaming to Foxglove Studio, plus ROS/ROS2 bridges that unify simulation and hardware pipelines.

### The Caveats
The SDK is released without any empirical evaluation or comparison to existing data‑logging tools, so its claimed performance and usefulness remain unverified.

## Kinect 2 Starter Kit

### The Breakthrough
The kit bundles a patched openFrameworks fork and the ofxKinectV2 addon, providing a ready‑to‑build Windows setup and an OSC server that streams per‑joint skeleton data on port 3001, simplifying cross‑platform Kinect V2 deployment.

### The Caveats
The repo offers no empirical evaluation or baseline comparison, so improvements in setup speed, latency, or reliability are unclear.

## quackd LLM Multi‑Robot CLI

### The Breakthrough
quackd abstracts robot control into ".duck" task files and a "flock" concept, integrates multiple LLM back‑ends (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, etc.) with ROS 2, and demonstrates a real‑world wave motion on an SO‑1101 arm driven by OpenAI’s gpt‑6‑astra via a simple CLI command.

### The Caveats
The only evaluation is a single‑arm demo; multi‑robot experiments or baseline comparisons are absent, leaving universal LLM‑driven orchestration claims unverified.

### Priority
Digit 5 stands out as the most tangible commercial humanoid with clear payload, runtime, and mass‑production specs, marking a major step toward scalable legged automation in warehouses.

### One action
Monitor Agility Robotics' upcoming field trials and compare Digit 5’s payload and endurance to your own warehouse automation requirements.

### What to watch
Both the 3D scene‑graph mobile manipulation system and the blind proprioceptive assembly work push perception‑driven manipulation forward: the former leverages foundation models for open‑set spatial memory, while the latter shows that joint‑only proprioception can transfer zero‑shot to real hardware. Watching benchmark comparisons and real‑world deployments will reveal which approach scales better for diverse manipulation tasks.
